title: Administrative and third-party records can help estimate who official systems miss
source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-38, an evaluation of experimental capture-recapture estimation using 2020 Census administrative and third-party records
geography: United States; 2020 Census address canvassing and nonresponse-followup operations, administrative records, third-party data, and post-enumeration coverage estimation

observations.period: 2020 Census evaluation experiments; paper published June 2026

denominator.unit: methodological evaluation of experimental administrative-record coverage estimation

administrative_use.value: the 2020 Census used administrative and third-party data in address canvassing and nonresponse followup

coverage_method.value: the report evaluates whether administrative and third-party records can support capture-recapture coverage estimates

estimation_approach.value: Expectation Maximization Log Linear Modeling was used, building on research from Statistics Netherlands and Statistics New Zealand

coverage_boundary.value: the work is experimental and documents evaluation results rather than a complete replacement for the independent post-enumeration survey and dual-system estimation approach

social_meaning.value: better record linkage may make undercount more visible, but it does not itself make a person counted, represented, protected, or able to contest an administrative decision

observations.method: The report evaluates an experimental capture-recapture approach using Census administrative and third-party data, with Expectation Maximization Log Linear Modeling, in the 2020 Census Program for Evaluation, Experiments, and Assessments.
observations.uncertainty: This is a Census CES working paper and methodological evaluation. The abstract does not provide a single national undercount estimate or establish that administrative records are complete, equally accurate across groups, privacy-neutral, or sufficient for official coverage measurement.
observations.subgroup: Addresses and people encountered through 2020 Census operations, administrative records, third-party data, and independent post-enumeration coverage methods; differential linkage and missingness by place, race, age, housing type, language, mobility, and legal or administrative status require separate audits.
observations.counterinterpretation: More records can improve coverage estimation while also importing stale, duplicated, mislinked, or unevenly available information. A better estimate of who was missed is not the same as successful enumeration, service access, political representation, or public trust.

related_sources.claim: The official report provides the experimental design, administrative and third-party data context, modeling approach, and evaluation boundaries.

boundary: This record adds a measurement-governance pathway from administrative records to coverage estimation. It does not establish a final population count, individual inclusion, privacy safety, equal linkage quality, representation, or downstream public protection.
